name: Complete GitHub sign-in
description: Runs on the callback leg only. The channel's oauth2_login block owns everything that is the same for every provider -- the 302 to GitHub, the signed state cookie and its CSRF binding, PKCE, and the code exchange -- and hands this workflow a verified grant at metadata.oauth; Orion retires the spent state cookie itself, so this response sets one cookie, not two. A SIGN-IN WHILE ANOTHER SESSION IS LIVE IS AN `account` NOTIFICATION, written after the session row and allowed to fail without failing the sign-in. THE SESSION IS SERVER-SIDE: `sid` names a row in `sessions`, written BEFORE the token is signed so a token can never name a row that does not exist, and its expires_at must stay in step with jwt_sign's expires_in. display_name is seeded from GitHub ON INSERT ONLY, because a competitor who renames themselves through PATCH /v1/me must not have it undone by their next sign-in. THE LOGIN IS RELEASED BEFORE IT IS CLAIMED: users.handle is unique, GitHub recycles logins, and the upsert alone cannot survive either half of a rename -- see the `release` task. WHERE IT SENDS YOU AFTERWARDS: `metadata.oauth.return_to` when the authorize leg carried a `?next=`, otherwise `app_url`. That value is NOT the caller's to choose freely -- Orion checks it against `oauth2_login.return_to.allow_list` on the authorize leg, seals it into the signed state cookie, and only hands it here once it comes back intact, so this workflow receives a vetted destination and an unlisted or tampered one simply is not there. The list is two origins (`app_return_url`, `console_return_url`) because the Orion console is a separate origin sharing this sign-in: without the return, a visitor sent from the console lands on the site and has to find their own way back.

tasks.name: Take the login back from the row that no longer holds it
tasks.description: GitHub gives one login to one account at a time, so a DIFFERENT github_id holding this login is provably stale -- a rename whose owner has not signed in since. Without this the upsert below collides on users_handle_uniq, unhandled, and the sign-in is a 500 that never clears: a new account can never take a freed login, and a rename into a held one can never land. The row is parked under `released.<github_id>`, a prefix containing a `.`, which a GitHub login cannot, so the tombstone can never collide with a real login or with a `baseline.` handle. github_id IS NOT NULL keeps a baseline out of it; after the reserved prefixes a baseline cannot collide anyway. SEPARATE FROM THE UPSERT ON PURPOSE: folded into it as a data-modifying CTE the two would share one command id, so the released row's old index entry is not reliably dead to the insert's uniqueness check -- which is the collision this exists to remove. The gap where nobody holds the login is harmless; two accounts swapping logins in the same instant can still collide, and that is a sign-in to retry rather than one that can never succeed.

input.query: UPDATE users SET handle = 'released.' || github_id WHERE lower(handle) = lower(($2)::text) AND github_id IS NOT NULL AND github_id <> ($1)::bigint
INSERT INTO users (github_id, handle, display_name) VALUES (($1)::bigint, ($2)::text, ($3)::text) ON CONFLICT (github_id) DO UPDATE SET handle = excluded.handle
SELECT id FROM users WHERE github_id = ($1)::bigint
INSERT INTO sessions (sid, user_id, expires_at, user_agent) VALUES (($1)::uuid, ($2)::uuid, now() + interval '30 days', ($3)::text)

tasks.name: Tell the account's other sessions about this one
tasks.description: Only when another session was already live: a first sign-in, or one after every other session ended, is not news to anyone. After record_session, so the new row exists and is excluded by sid rather than by time. continue_on_error, because a notification must never be the reason a sign-in fails -- the cookie below is the whole point of this workflow. Keyed on the new sid, which is minted once per sign-in, so a retried request cannot say it twice.

input.query: INSERT INTO notifications (user_id, category, kind, tone, subject, description, link, data, dedupe_key) SELECT u.id, 'account', 'account', 'info', 'New sign-in to your account', 'Signed in from ' || coalesce(left(nullif(btrim(($3)::text), ''), 300), 'a browser that did not name itself') || '. If this was not you, end that session.', '/me/account', jsonb_build_object('sid', ($1)::uuid, 'user_agent', left(($3)::text, 300)), 'sign-in:' || ($1)::uuid FROM users u WHERE u.id = ($2)::uuid AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM live_sessions ls WHERE ls.user_id = u.id AND ls.sid <> ($1)::uuid) AND notification_wanted(u.id, 'account') ON CONFLICT (user_id, dedupe_key) DO NOTHING
